newsitem.title: GERMANY: AgrEvo expects to launch herbicide in US next year. [CORRECTED 18:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: AgrEvo expects to launch herbicide in US next year. [CORRECTED 18:00 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects to make clear that the Liberty herbicide is not itself genetically altered, but is for use on genetically-altered feeds.)
German crop protection group AgrEvo said on Friday it expects to introduce its herbicide Liberty in the United States and Europe in the next two years.

"We expect to be able to use Liberty for maize for the 1997 planting season in the U.S. and we expect it will be introduced into Europe in late 1997 or early 1998," AgrEvo board member Juergen Asshauer said.
The herbicide is for use on genetically-altered feeds modified for resistance to the active ingredient glufosinat for selective weed control.

Liberty, based on the active ingredient glufosinat, is intended for selective application in maize and soybean crops in the U.S. and has been been introduced for use on rapeseed in Canada to control grass weed.
AgrEvo, the world's second largest crop protection company, is jointly owned by Frankfurt-based chemicals and drugs group Hoechst AG and Berlin-based drugs group Schering AG.
AgrEvo expects Liberty sales will significantly contribute to its results in the coming years.
Asshauer added that European import restrictions on food treated with Liberty would also soon be lifted.

Germans have been particularly pre-occupied with the risks associated with genetic engineering and a small group has launched an active campaign to block the introduction of such products in recent years, Asshauer said.
